findings.summary: The contract makes the governed-by-nothing escape a FIXED VERBATIM sentence precisely so the check is a grep, but no shipping skill quotes the sentence — the author (plan) is told only to "write that sentence explicitly", and both readers (go, audit) are told to judge prose intent ("says in so many words", "the plan should say in ## Approach that this phase is governed by nothing").
findings.why_it_matters: contracts/phase-plan.md does not ship; skills are self-contained. An agent finalizing a plan writes its own wording ("No knowledge docs apply here."). The grep the contract promises then fails, and the only enforcement left is exactly the prose-intent judgement the contract calls "the one non-computable test in a system built on computable state." The mandatory half of a mandatory section is enforced by nothing computable.
findings.fix: Paste the exact string — `Governed by: none — no `knowledge/` or `decisions/` document constrains this phase.` — into all three skills: plan step 3 (write this line, verbatim, nothing else), go Step 3 (presence of this line, matched literally, is the only thing that satisfies the missing-section branch), and audit (replace "says in so many words" with a literal-string check).

findings.summary: The neighbour check restricts the sibling read to "`## Objective` + `## Scope` (those two sections only)", yet its second admission route needs "either plan's prose" forward pointers and its silencing rule needs to see whether a pointer "already names an owner" — and seams, by the check's own resolution rule, are written into `## Approach`.
findings.why_it_matters: Following the read limit literally, an agent can never see a sibling's forward pointer or a seam already written in the sibling's `## Approach`. Route 2 becomes half-dead on the sibling side, and — worse — an overlap resolved last time by writing the seam into the sibling is re-detected as a fresh hit on every re-finalize, breaking the explicit promise that a written seam is "silent forever after, including on a re-finalize." Repeated false hits are the rubber-stamp failure the design is written against.
findings.fix: Change the sibling read-set to `## Objective` + `## Scope` + `## Approach` (still no code, still no other milestone), and say why: Approach is where a written seam and a resolved forward pointer live, so it is the section that makes a hit silent. Mirror the change in ARCHITECTURE.md's neighbour-check paragraph.

findings.summary: Audit's admission bar reads "the same deliverable claimed twice, or a cross-reference already sitting in either plan's prose" — it drops the qualifier that makes plan's route 2 work (an *unresolved* pointer; one that names an owner is a written seam and is silent).
findings.why_it_matters: The prescribed resolution for a genuine overlap is to write the seam into `## Approach` — a cross-reference naming an owner. Audit as written then reports every correctly-resolved overlap as a finding, and routes the user back to `plan` to re-resolve what is already resolved. The grader punishes conformance, which is worse than not grading it.
findings.fix: Restate audit's second route as plan's: "a forward pointer in either plan's prose that names an unexecuted sibling *without saying who owns the work*; a pointer that already names an owner is a written seam and is not a finding." Add the subtraction test as the stated bar for the first route too, so audit and plan grade the same thing.

findings.summary: Nothing says a `## Governed by` heading with zero entries is malformed: the contract requires "either the section or the sentence", audit checks "the section is present", and go only stops on a path that fails to resolve.
findings.why_it_matters: A finalize pass under time pressure writes the empty heading, every gate passes, `go` reads nothing, and the section "dies quietly" — the exact failure the mandatory rule was written to prevent — while the plan looks conformant to the grader. It also erases the distinction the fixed sentence exists to make: governed-by-nothing asserted deliberately vs. never filled in.
findings.fix: Add a rule to contracts/phase-plan.md and to audit's grade: a `## Governed by` section with no entries is malformed — a phase governed by nothing carries the fixed sentence in `## Approach` and no section at all. Add the same branch to go Step 3 (empty section → same stop as a dangling path).

findings.summary: The subtraction test admits a hit on "No, **or only partly**", but the three resolutions offered are whole-item ones — this plan owns it, the sibling owns it (**drop it here**), or write the seam.
findings.why_it_matters: On a partial hit (the sibling leaves the artifact half-way there), "the sibling owns it — drop it here" silently deletes the remainder from the only plan that named it. The change is aimed at work built twice and introduces a path to work built zero times, which is the more expensive failure and the harder one to notice.
findings.fix: Split the resolution by hit type: a total hit resolves to owner-or-drop; a *partial* hit has exactly two legal resolutions — narrow this scope item to the remainder and name in `## Approach` what the sibling leaves behind, or take the whole item here and drop it from the sibling. A bare drop on a partial hit is forbidden.

findings.summary: "The sibling owns it" and "the seam is written into `## Approach`" never say *whose* plan file gets edited, nor whether a sibling that is itself finalized-and-unexecuted may be edited.
findings.why_it_matters: Auto-finalize keeps siblings as drafts in the common case, but a manually finalized sibling is reachable (the check's reach is all unticked siblings, regardless of state). Editing a finalized plan changes what `go` will build with no freshness check to catch it — checkpoint forbids exactly this elsewhere in the system for exactly this reason. An agent hits the branch with two documents pointing opposite ways and has to guess.
findings.fix: State the rule: resolution edits *this* plan; a draft sibling may be edited too; a **finalized** sibling is never edited in place — if it must change, say so and re-finalize it through the normal pass. Say which plan carries the seam sentence when both stay (this one, always, so the check is single-writer).

findings.summary: "Every hit resolves before finalize" is absolute, but "more than three means the milestone's phase cut is wrong — say so and propose a re-cut, rather than filing a list of items" tells the agent not to work the hits; nothing says whether finalize proceeds, and nothing covers the user declining the re-cut.
findings.why_it_matters: An agent with four hits has two instructions it cannot both obey and no stated exit. It will improvise — most likely resolve three, mention the fourth, and finalize — producing the "reported but not resolved" outcome the same paragraph calls not a pass.
findings.fix: Make the >3 branch a hard stop with a named state: finalize does not complete; present the re-cut proposal and stop. If the user declines the re-cut, the check reverts to normal — every hit resolves individually before finalize completes. Mirror in ARCHITECTURE.md.

findings.summary: "Unexecuted = its `milestone.md` `## Phases` entry is unticked" is now a State Determination row, but a plan file in `phases/` with no entry in `## Phases` (or a milestone whose `milestone.md` has no `## Phases` yet) is neither ticked nor unticked.
findings.why_it_matters: The just-authored plan set is exactly where entries lag the files, and the neighbour check runs at that moment. The agent must guess whether an entry-less sibling is in reach; guessing "out" silently disables the check for the newest and most likely-overlapping plan. The same hole now propagates to the pivot sweep and to audit, which both key off this definition.
findings.fix: Complete the definition in the State Determination row: a phase-plan file with no `## Phases` entry counts as **unexecuted** (in reach), and the missing entry is itself a structural finding routed to checkpoint. Reference that row from plan and audit instead of restating the short form.

findings.summary: Step 3 rules only the duplication case — "if a rule appears both in the plan and in the doc it points at, the doc is the one that is current" — and says nothing about the case the whole section exists to catch: the governing doc forbids what `## Approach` (approved at finalize) tells `go` to do.
findings.why_it_matters: `go` is a thin executor forbidden from re-proposing and forbidden from choosing a reading of an ambiguous scope. Faced with rule-vs-approach it has no exit: the two-exit escape hatch covers scope-vs-code contradictions, not plan-vs-rule. The agent either follows the approved approach (making the read ceremonial — the exact inertness this change exists to fix) or silently overrides an approved approach.
findings.fix: Add a third case to Step 3: if a document `## Governed by` names forbids or contradicts what `## Approach` directs, that is the *not satisfiable as written* exit — name the rule, the path, and the approach step that conflicts, build nothing further, and route to `/scaffold-checkpoint`. `go` never picks between the rule and the approach.

findings.summary: Audit is told to "flag a plan that **pastes a `knowledge/` rule's content** instead of pointing at it", but the contract simultaneously requires `## Approach` to state "how the rule applies to this phase" — and nothing draws the line between applying and copying.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a grader criterion with no rule a grader can apply. In practice it becomes either a no-op (never fired) or a noise generator that flags the required application sentence, and audit's findings are what users act on. It is the same defect class the change is fixing — an instruction obeyed exactly and still leaving the decision unmade.
findings.fix: Give it a computable signature or drop it from audit: flag only (a) a heading or lead-in enumerating rules (e.g. "the rules this plan leans on"), or (b) a passage that restates a governed-by doc's rule statement without tying it to this phase's work. Say explicitly that a sentence saying how the rule applies here is required, never a finding.

findings.summary: "The next two or three unticked entries *after* the active one" has no defined behaviour when there is no active phase — `## Next` silent or dangling, both of which `status`'s own health check anticipates — and it also leaves the 2-vs-3 choice unruled (ARCHITECTURE says "up to three").
findings.why_it_matters: The silent/dangling cursor is precisely the session where the user most needs to see the queue, and it is the branch where the agent has no anchor and will either omit the section or invent one. The unruled count makes output non-deterministic between sessions for no gain.
findings.fix: State the fallback: with no resolvable active phase, list the first three unticked `## Phases` entries in order and say the cursor is lost. Replace "two or three" with "up to three" in both places so the skill matches ARCHITECTURE.md, and add that unticked entries *before* the active one are listed too (a skipped phase is the thing worth seeing).

findings.summary: The finalize pass tells the author to "write that sentence explicitly into `## Approach`" for a phase governed by nothing, but the skill never states the sentence — the fixed wording exists only in contracts/phase-plan.md, which does not ship.
findings.why_it_matters: contracts/phase-plan.md:88 mandates the exact line "Governed by: none — no `knowledge/` or `decisions/` document constrains this phase." precisely so the finalized-plan check is a grep and not a judgement about prose (contract lines 80-91, 153-155). scaffold-plan is the only skill that WRITES it, and "that sentence" has no antecedent anywhere in the skill file — grep shows the string "Governed by: none" appears in the repo only in the contract. A user's agent finalizing a plan with no governing docs will invent its own wording, so audit's and go's checks fall back to prose judgement — the one non-computable test the change exists to eliminate.
findings.fix: In scaffold-plan Step 3 of the finalize pass, quote the sentence verbatim as a blockquote and say it is fixed wording, not a paraphrase: "> Governed by: none — no `knowledge/` or `decisions/` document constrains this phase."

findings.summary: Audit accepts "`## Approach` says in so many words that the phase is governed by no `knowledge/` or `decisions/` document" instead of grading the contract's verbatim sentence.
findings.why_it_matters: skills/scaffold-audit/SKILL.md:119-120 vs contracts/phase-plan.md:84-91, which fixes the wording explicitly "because a grader that has to judge prose intent is the one non-computable test in a system built on computable state" and says "Its presence is a `grep`". Audit is the grader that ships verbatim contract copies precisely to grade exactly; "in so many words" reintroduces the judgement the contract rules out, so two audits of the same plan can disagree, and a plan with a hand-waved approach paragraph passes.
findings.fix: Replace "says in so many words that the phase is governed by no `knowledge/` or `decisions/` document" with a grep for the exact line, quoted: `## Approach` contains verbatim "Governed by: none — no `knowledge/` or `decisions/` document constrains this phase."; anything else is malformed.

findings.summary: go's read-set step accepts any prose claim ("the plan should say in `## Approach` that this phase is governed by nothing. If it does, proceed") rather than the contract's verbatim line.
findings.why_it_matters: skills/scaffold-go/SKILL.md:126-127. go is the reader that makes the pointer real, and it is the same grep the contract specifies (contracts/phase-plan.md:88-91). With no fixed string, go's "if it does, proceed" is a judgement call on prose — and since scaffold-plan never writes a fixed string either (see verbatim-governed-by-none-sentence-missing-from-plan), the three skills' notions of "says it is governed by nothing" cannot be relied on to agree.
findings.fix: Quote the fixed sentence in go's Step 3 and make the test a literal match: proceed only if `## Approach` carries "Governed by: none — no `knowledge/` or `decisions/` document constrains this phase."

findings.summary: For a finalized plan carrying neither `## Governed by` nor the governed-by-nothing sentence, go asks "Re-finalize … or continue?" — behaviour the spec does not state and the contract calls malformed.
findings.why_it_matters: skills/scaffold-go/SKILL.md:126-130. contracts/phase-plan.md:155 and 204-205 grade that plan as malformed, and go stops hard on every other malformed-plan signal (a draft, a stale stamp, an unresolvable `## Governed by` path at go's own lines 122-125). An agent following it executes a plan the contract declares malformed, and the one obligation the change exists to guarantee (the rules were actually read) is silently skipped.
findings.fix: Either make it a stop consistent with the other malformed-plan cases, or — if the intent is a transition allowance for plans that predate the read-set — state that allowance in ARCHITECTURE.md's `/scaffold-go` bullet first and have the skill cite it, since the spec is the source.

findings.summary: The Execution model says plans "can go stale two ways, and each has a defense", and the very next bullet calls plan-set coherence "the third staleness obligation" — the count contradicts itself, and scaffold-checkpoint depends on that count.

findings.summary: scaffold-plan justifies section placement with "checkpoint's sweep checks order", but checkpoint's structural check grades order "per the shapes in Step 5" and Step 5 contains no phase-plan shape.
findings.why_it_matters: skills/scaffold-plan/SKILL.md:301 vs skills/scaffold-checkpoint/SKILL.md:304 ("Required sections present, correctly named, and in order (per the shapes in Step 5)"); checkpoint Step 5 covers milestone.md, state.md, knowledge/, architecture.md, project.md and roadmap.md only — no Objective/Scope/Approach/Acceptance/Governed by/Targets ordering exists there, and checkpoint is deliberately barred from re-enumerating contract details. So a mis-ordered `## Governed by` is caught only by `/scaffold-audit`, and plan cites a backstop that isn't there.
findings.fix: Change the parenthetical in scaffold-plan step 4 to name the real grader — "(the contract fixes the section order: Acceptance, Governed by, Targets, and `/scaffold-audit` grades it)" — rather than checkpoint.

findings.summary: The fixed verbatim "governed by nothing" sentence that the contract defines exists in no shipping skill — plan, go and audit all describe it as free prose, turning a grep into a judgement call.
findings.why_it_matters: contracts/phase-plan.md fixes the exact wording ("Governed by: none — no `knowledge/` or `decisions/` document constrains this phase.") precisely so the check is computable. But scaffold-plan says only "write that sentence explicitly into ## Approach" (which sentence?), scaffold-go says "the plan should say in ## Approach that this phase is governed by nothing", and scaffold-audit says "## Approach says in so many words". Skills ship alone, so a stranger finalizing a phase with no governing docs writes something like "No knowledge docs apply here." — then go and audit have to judge prose intent, which is exactly the non-computable test the design forbids. Two agents will disagree on the same plan. This is the skills being wrong against the spec, not the spec being wrong.
findings.fix: Put the literal sentence in all three skills. In scaffold-plan finalize step 3: "write this line verbatim into ## Approach — the wording is fixed so the check is a grep, not a judgement: `Governed by: none — no knowledge/ or decisions/ document constrains this phase.`" In scaffold-go step 3, replace the prose test with "## Approach contains that exact line → proceed". In scaffold-audit's ## Governed by bullet, replace "says in so many words" with the same verbatim string.

findings.summary: The finalize pass never tells you to enumerate .scaffold/knowledge/ and .scaffold/decisions/, and it explicitly bypasses the Phase 1 triage that does.
findings.why_it_matters: "On --final … run the Finalize pass below **instead of** the ordinary author flow" — so Phase 1's "any knowledge/ doc relevant to the direction. Scan decisions/ and investigations/ by filename" is skipped on the one invocation that must produce ## Governed by. Finalize step 3 says "List the knowledge/ and decisions/ documents whose rules bind this phase" but names no step that puts the candidate set in front of you. Invoked cold with `/scaffold-plan --final`, I have read state.md, roadmap.md, the plan, and code — I have never listed either folder. The likely outcomes are an empty section or the verbatim "governed by none" line on a phase that is in fact governed, which no downstream check can catch (go and audit only verify that listed paths resolve; neither can detect an omission).
findings.fix: Add a first sub-step to finalize step 3: "List every file in `.scaffold/knowledge/` and `.scaffold/decisions/` (filenames plus each doc's opening rule/ruling line — read any that could plausibly bind). That listing is the candidate set; the section is chosen from it, never from memory."

findings.summary: "Documents whose rules bind this phase" is defined only by exclusions — there is no positive, operational test for binds-vs-merely-relates, unlike the subtraction test one step above it.
findings.why_it_matters: Finalize step 3 tells me what is *not* eligible (spec, sibling plan, source files) but never how to rule on the eligible set. On a real project with four knowledge docs, three arguably touch the phase: a tenancy invariant the phase's queries must respect (clearly binds), a naming-convention doc (maybe), an ADR choosing the job runner the phase happens to use (maybe). With no test, one agent lists one path and another lists all eight ADRs — and an over-listed section is not harmless: go must read every listed document in full before the first deliverable, so a padded read-set burns the execution session's context, which is the resource the one-agent-session phase rule is protecting. Note the contrast: the neighbour check one step earlier gives a crisp counterfactual test plus an artifact-naming admission bar; this section gives nothing comparable.
findings.fix: Add a membership test mirroring the subtraction test: "One test per candidate: **if you built this phase in violation of this document's rule, would the phase be wrong?** Yes → it binds, list it. If the rule is merely about the same area, or the phase could violate it and still be correct, it does not bind — leave it out. Note the rule, not the doc's topic, in the trailing few words; if you cannot name the rule, it does not belong."

findings.summary: The neighbour check reads only siblings' ## Objective + ## Scope, so a seam previously resolved into a sibling's ## Approach is invisible and the same overlap is re-reported as a hit on every re-finalize.
findings.why_it_matters: Step 2 hard-caps the read at two sections ("those two sections only… Reach stops there"), but the prescribed resolution for a genuine shared touch is "## Approach states the seam", and the step's own second admission route promises a written seam is "never re-reported on a re-finalize". Both cannot be true when the seam was written into the sibling. Concretely: 07 and 08 both touch the exporter, 07's finalize writes the seam into 08's ## Approach and drops the item from 07's scope. Phase 09 re-finalizes later with 08 still unticked; it reads 08's Objective+Scope, sees the exporter deliverable, cannot see the seam, and files it as a hit again. The agent then "resolves" an already-resolved overlap — most likely by deleting the item from one plan, which is how work goes missing.
findings.fix: Extend the read for the seam case only: "Read each unexecuted sibling's ## Objective + ## Scope. On a candidate hit — and only then — also read that sibling's ## Approach: a seam already written there (naming who owns the work and what the other assumes) is a resolved overlap, not a hit, and is not re-reported."

findings.summary: Resolving a hit can require editing a sibling plan, and the step says neither whose ## Approach gets the seam nor what happens when that sibling is already finalized.
findings.why_it_matters: "both genuinely touch it and `## Approach` states the seam" leaves the owning document unnamed, and "the sibling owns it (drop it here)" only covers this plan's edit. If the seam goes into a sibling that carries ## Targets, the contract's own rule — "Rewriting a finalized plan DEMOTES it to draft — delete ## Targets in the same edit" (it names scope, approach *or* acceptance) — is triggered, and the neighbour check says nothing about it. A stranger will either (a) silently edit a finalized sibling's ## Approach and leave its stamp standing, so go later executes a plan whose approach changed after its approval seam, or (b) demote a sibling the user never asked to touch, without telling them. Auto-finalize makes case (a) reachable in normal use: siblings stay drafts by default, but any earlier finalized-and-not-yet-run sibling is exactly this case.
findings.fix: State the ownership and the demotion rule: "Write the seam into **this** plan's ## Approach by default — you are the plan being finalized. If the seam only makes sense in the sibling, and that sibling carries ## Targets, editing it demotes it: delete its ## Targets in the same edit, say so, and report it as `rewritten → draft` needing `--final` before `go`. Say it at step 7's confirmation seam before you make the edit."

findings.summary: "More than three [hits] means the milestone's phase cut is wrong — say so and propose a re-cut" does not say whether the finalize pass stops there or continues.
findings.why_it_matters: The two outcomes are materially different: either I abandon the finalize (no ## Governed by, no ## Targets written, state.md untouched) and wait for a ruling on the re-cut, or I resolve the hits anyway and finalize a plan whose milestone I just declared mis-cut. Every other stop in this skill is explicit ("Wait.", "STOP. Wait for Adam's explicit approval."), so the silence here reads as deliberate to someone who watched the design and as an oversight to a stranger. The re-cut is also a Phase 4a-shaped decision, which normally has its own confirmation.
findings.fix: Add the halt: "More than three hits: stop the finalize — write nothing — report that the cut is wrong, propose the re-cut, and wait. Finalize resumes after the plans are re-authored."

findings.summary: "the next two or three unticked entries" leaves the count to the agent, in both Step 4 and Step 5.
findings.why_it_matters: Nothing distinguishes a two-entry answer from a three-entry one, so the same milestone briefs differently between sessions and the user cannot tell whether a third phase exists or was simply not shown — which undercuts the stated purpose of the line (spotting an overlap or a mis-ordered cut without holding the plan set in memory).
findings.fix: Say "up to three" in both places: "the next unticked entries after the active one, up to three, by title, in checklist order (fewer if fewer remain)."

findings.summary: Nothing in the new read-set text rules on the *status* of a `decisions/` doc, so `## Governed by` may point at a Superseded or Proposed ADR and `go` is instructed to execute under it as binding law.
findings.why_it_matters: `contracts/decision.md` line 31 defines `**Status:** Accepted | Superseded by [[NNNN-…]] | Proposed`, and superseded ADRs are explicitly kept on disk ("architecturally-significant ones are kept with a `Superseded` status instead"). So a superseded ADR path resolves, exists on disk, and lives under `.scaffold/decisions/` — it passes every test the new text defines: plan's binding test ("if you built this phase in violation of this document's rule, would the phase be wrong?" — yes, by the dead rule), audit's grade ("a repo-relative path under `.scaffold/knowledge/` or `.scaffold/decisions/` that **exists on disk**"), and go's read step, which says "read the whole document… a rule the plan points at is a rule you are executing under." The realistic path is worse than an authoring slip: a plan finalized against ADR 0007 is superseded by ADR 0012 a week later; the freshness gate exempts everything under `.scaffold/`, so the plan stays *final & fresh*, and `go` now reads a dead ruling in full and builds to it. Worse, the new contradiction branch actively fires the wrong way — if the *live* code follows ADR 0012, go sees the superseded rule "forbid what the approach directs" and hard-stops the phase on a rule that no longer exists. Scaffold already gates this channel everywhere else ("a plan is never authored on a not-yet-approved ADR"; checkpoint's "every cited ADR exists and isn't silently superseded"), which is exactly why the omission here is invisible: the new pointer is a second citation channel with none of the gate.
findings.fix: Add the status rule in all three places. Contract, under "What belongs": a `decisions/` entry must be an **Accepted** ADR — a `Proposed` one is the ADR gate (resolve it first) and a `Superseded` one points at the superseding ADR instead; add the matching anti-pattern. plan step 3: after the binding test, "read the candidate's `**Status:**` line — list it only if Accepted; a Superseded entry is replaced by its successor, a Proposed one resolves through the ADR gate (Phase 3) before finalize completes." go Step 3: a listed decision whose Status is not `Accepted` stops `go` with its own message ("`## Governed by` names `<path>`, whose status is `Superseded by 0012`. Re-finalize with `/scaffold-plan --final`.") rather than being read as binding. audit: add it to the per-entry grade alongside exists-on-disk.

findings.summary: Three new passages declare that a plan file with no `milestone.md` `## Phases` entry is "a structural finding for `checkpoint`" and tell the agent to hand it there, but checkpoint's structural and coherence lists contain no such check.
findings.why_it_matters: The fix for the undefined-unexecuted case created an obligation with no owner. ARCHITECTURE's new State Determination row says "the missing entry is a structural finding for `checkpoint`"; plan's neighbour check says "note the missing entry for `/scaffold-checkpoint` to add"; audit says "the missing entry is a structural finding of its own". Checkpoint's Step 7 structural list checks only (1) required sections present and in order per the Step 5 shapes, (2) frontmatter, (3) Law violations — and is explicitly told "don't re-enumerate them here; route them to audit." Its coherence item 6, Active-cursor sanity, checks only that `## Next` points at a plan that exists and that *the named phase* is consistent with the checklist — it never walks `phases/*.md` looking for unlisted files. So an agent following plan's instruction literally writes the note into its summary, checkpoint receives it, finds no check it belongs to, and Step 7b's disposition test ("could a later run re-derive this from disk?") sends it to "reporting it is exit enough" — the entry is never added. The plan stays unlisted, and it stays permanently in the neighbour check's and audit's reach as a phantom sibling, which is precisely the state the new definition was written to make finite. The Skill × Artifact table row for `…/phases/NN-slug.md` under checkpoint still reads "× (done; tick lands in `milestone.md`)", confirming checkpoint is not given the artifact at all.
findings.fix: Add the check to checkpoint's structural list (or coherence item 6): "**Every plan file is listed.** Each `milestones/NN-slug/phases/*.md` in a live milestone has an entry in that `milestone.md`'s `## Phases`; add the missing unticked entry in list position — this is a Fixed-class finding, not a route." Update the Skill × Artifact row for `…/phases/NN-slug.md` under `checkpoint` from `×` to note the listing check, so the spec and the skill agree on who owns it.

findings.summary: The plan-set coherence invariant was added as a Rules bullet and an Anti-pattern in the phase-plan contract, but audit's conformance pass grades one plan at a time against that contract and cannot evaluate a rule about *other* plans — and nothing tells the grader to mark it n-a.
findings.why_it_matters: Audit Step 2 dispatches a fresh subagent per doc and instructs it to "**Walk the contract line by line** — every item in its Required structure, every bullet in **Rules**, and every entry in **Anti-patterns**. For *each* one, emit an explicit verdict — pass / fail / n-a", with "**Every anti-pattern is checked by name**; you may not drop one because the doc 'seems clean.'" The two new entries — "No two unexecuted plans in a milestone claim the same deliverable" and "Two unexecuted plans in one milestone claiming the same deliverable with no seam written" — are unanswerable from the graded file: the agent has one plan, no siblings, and no `milestone.md` tick state. The n-a escape as written applies to a whole contract that doesn't fit the file type ("A contract whose `type` doesn't apply to a given file"), not to a rule that outruns the pass, so the literal reading is that the grader must fetch siblings itself and duplicate the reality pass — or emit fail. And since "conforms only if every rule passed", an unresolvable verdict downgrades every phase plan in the tree, and conformance *gates* the reality pass where the real coherence check lives. Note the contract itself half-sees this — "This rule is the grade; `scaffold-plan` carries the full procedure" — but a grader told to walk every bullet has no license to skip it.
findings.fix: Mark the rule's scope in the contract text itself, e.g. append to the Rules bullet: "**Graded across plans, not on one plan** — a per-document conformance grade marks this n-a; it is checked by `scaffold-plan`'s neighbour check at finalize and by `/scaffold-audit`'s reality pass." Do the same on the anti-pattern, and add the corresponding n-a license to audit Step 2 ("a rule whose subject is *other* documents is n-a for the per-doc pass").

findings.summary: Both new ARCHITECTURE passages still describe the neighbour check's read set as `## Objective` + `## Scope` and still offer the bare-drop resolution trio — two things the shipping skill now deliberately contradicts, leaving the source rotted against the derived artifact.
findings.why_it_matters: CLAUDE.md makes the direction one-way ("Change the design in the spec, then propagate to the skills — never hack a skill and let the spec rot into stale parallel notes"), so an agent reading the spec as authority reconstructs the *broken* check. Two concrete divergences, both introduced by fixes that landed only in the skill. (1) Read set: ARCHITECTURE says "read the `## Objective` and `## Scope` of every unexecuted sibling plan" (Execution model) and "reads the `## Objective` and `## Scope`" (/scaffold-plan section); the skill now reads "`## Objective` + `## Scope` + `## Approach` (those three sections only)" and states why — "`## Approach` is in the set because that is where a written seam and an owned forward pointer live: without it… you re-report it on every re-finalize." A spec-faithful implementation re-reports every resolved seam forever. (2) Resolutions: ARCHITECTURE offers "this plan owns it, the sibling owns it, or both touch it and the seam goes into `## Approach`" for a hit it now admits on "No, **or only partly**" — the exact whole-item trio the skill's new partial-hit rule forbids ("A bare drop here is forbidden — it deletes the remainder from the only plan that named it, and the work gets built zero times"). ARCHITECTURE also never carries the "whose file the edit lands in" ruling at all.
findings.fix: Propagate both fixes upward: change the read set in both ARCHITECTURE passages to `## Objective` + `## Scope` + `## Approach` with the one-clause reason (Approach carries the written seam), and split the resolution list by answer as the skill does — whole hit → one plan owns it; partial hit → narrow to the remainder or take the whole item, never a bare drop; plus the seam sentence lands in the plan being finalized and a finalized sibling is never edited in place.

findings.summary: The neighbour check is step 2 and is framed "before you commit to a scope", but step 5 ("Tighten Scope/Approach against what the code actually is") and step 6 (the stranger test) then change the scope, and nothing says to re-run the check against the scope actually written.
findings.why_it_matters: The check is per scope item — "Per scope item, one test: if that sibling executed first…" — so its result is only as good as the item list it saw. Step 5 explicitly rewrites that list against the code, which is where scope items get split, merged, or added ("this needs a migration step too"), and step 6 adds material to `## Approach`. An item introduced at step 5 is never subtraction-tested against any sibling, and it is exactly the high-risk kind: code-derived, so the sibling's author likely derived the same item from the same code. That is the authoring-time duplication this whole change exists to catch, entering through the one door the check doesn't watch. An agent following the numbered steps literally has no instruction to look back, and step 7 then presents an approach whose newest items were never checked. Note the two other finalize-written sections have explicit re-run discipline ("on a *re*-finalize, **replace** the existing section") while this one has none.
findings.fix: Either move the check after step 5 (finalize the scope, then check it), or add a closing clause to step 2: "Re-run the subtraction test on any scope item that step 5's tightening adds or materially re-cuts — an item derived from the code is the likeliest one a sibling derived too." Given step 2's "before you commit to a scope" framing, the cleaner edit is the re-run clause plus a pointer from step 5 back to it.

findings.summary: "Coming up" takes only unticked entries *after* the active one, so an unticked phase that sits earlier in `## Phases` than the cursor is invisible — even though it is unexecuted, in the neighbour check's reach, and in audit's coherence reach.
findings.why_it_matters: The section's stated justification is overlap visibility — "nothing else in the system shows the shape of what is queued" and "it lets the user spot an overlap or a mis-ordered cut without holding the whole plan set in memory" — but its window is defined positionally against a cursor that scaffold explicitly does not tie to list order (`## Next` is the active marker; ARCHITECTURE: "Active = wherever `state.md` Next points (not folder order)"). An earlier phase left unticked — abandoned mid-phase by checkpoint, parked on a `[USER]` deliverable, or inserted late by a re-cut — is unexecuted by the very State Determination row this change added ("**Unexecuted** = unticked **or absent**"), so `plan`'s neighbour check and `audit`'s plan-set check both walk it while `status` silently drops it. The user sees a three-line queue that omits the one plan most likely to be stale or duplicated, and the output item 3 skip rule compounds it ("skip if the active phase is the last unticked one") — with a stranded earlier phase, that skip hides the queue entirely.
findings.fix: Define the window over the unexecuted set rather than position: "up to three unticked entries, in list order, starting after the active one; if any unticked entry sits *before* the active one, name it first and mark it stranded — it is unexecuted and in the neighbour check's reach even though the cursor has moved past it." Adjust the item-3 skip rule to fire only when no unticked entry other than the active one exists anywhere in the list.

findings.summary: Both computable signatures for a pasted rule presuppose the plan already points at the doc, so the exact defect the read-set exists to kill — pasting a `knowledge/` rule *instead of* listing it in `## Governed by` — matches neither.
findings.why_it_matters: Signature (b) is "a passage that restates **a `## Governed by` doc's** rule statement without naming any of this phase's own scope items, files, or steps" — scoped to docs the plan already listed. Signature (a) is a lead-in heading ("the rules this plan leans on", "rules that apply here"). A plan that quietly inlines two sentences of a knowledge rule into `## Approach` with no lead-in and no corresponding `## Governed by` entry hits neither: (a) has nothing to key on, and (b)'s corpus is empty for that doc. That plan passes every check in the diff — the section is present with at least one entry, every listed path resolves — while carrying a second, unpointed home for a rule, which the contract's own diagnosis calls "the one that goes stale." Since the stated payoff of the whole change is deflation ("once the pointer is honoured by `go`, the paste is redundant"), the grader that is supposed to enforce deflation only inspects plans that already did the right thing, and the plans that didn't are graded clean.
findings.fix: Widen (b)'s corpus from the plan's own `## Governed by` list to the milestone-relevant `knowledge/`+`decisions/` set audit already inventories at Step 1: "a passage that restates the rule statement of **any** `.scaffold/knowledge/` or `.scaffold/decisions/` doc without naming this phase's own scope items, files, or steps — and if that doc is not in `## Governed by`, the finding is doubled: an unpointed rule was copied rather than listed."

findings.summary: "If a finalized sibling must change, say so and re-finalize it through the normal pass" never says whether the current finalize completes, and a sibling re-finalize would itself run a neighbour check back against the plan being finalized.
findings.why_it_matters: The "Whose file the edit lands in" paragraph fixed who may be edited but not what happens next, and it collides with the rule directly above it — "**Every hit resolves before finalize.** … Reporting an overlap without resolving it is not a pass." An agent that lands on a hit whose only legal resolution is a change to a finalized, unexecuted sibling has three unruled branches: finish this finalize with the hit unresolved (forbidden by the rule above), stop like the >3 hard stop (only that one case is defined as a hard stop), or re-finalize the sibling now — which re-enters the same finalize pass, runs step 2 against *this* plan (still mid-finalize, its scope not yet written to disk, so the sibling reads the pre-edit version), and re-stamps the sibling's `## Targets` against code the user is not being asked about. The >3 branch was given an explicit ruling in this round precisely because a hard stop must be stated; this branch was left without one.
findings.fix: State the branch alongside the others: a hit whose only legal resolution changes a *finalized* sibling is a hard stop of the same kind — finalize does not complete, this plan stays a draft, name the sibling and the item, and re-finalize the sibling first; then re-run this finalize from step 1 against the sibling as written. That keeps one plan mid-finalize at a time and removes the mutual-recursion case.

findings.summary: Audit's plan-set coherence check reads only `## Objective` + `## Scope` of the unexecuted plans, yet both of its silencing conditions live in `## Approach` and in "either plan's prose" — the identical defect that was already fixed in scaffold-plan's neighbour check by widening its read to three sections.
findings.why_it_matters: Audit's own text says "grade exactly what `plan`'s neighbour check grades, or you punish conformance" — but it cannot see what plan writes. The prescribed resolution for a hit is a seam sentence in `## Approach` (plan finalize step 2: "The seam sentence always goes in **this** plan"), and the forward-pointer route is silenced only when the pointer "already names an owner" — both invisible in an Objective+Scope read. Every plan pair that was resolved conformantly at finalize is re-flagged by audit as a plan-set coherence finding, and the finding routes back to `plan`, which will re-open a seam it already wrote. This is the exact conformance-punishing false positive the admission bar exists to prevent.
findings.fix: In the plan-set coherence bullet, change the read set to `## Objective` + `## Scope` + `## Approach` (those three sections only) and say why, matching skills/scaffold-plan/SKILL.md finalize step 2: `## Approach` is where a written seam and an owned forward pointer live, so without it a resolved overlap is re-reported on every audit.

findings.summary: ARCHITECTURE describes the neighbour check's read set as `## Objective` and `## Scope` in both places it states it (Execution model → Plan-set coherence, ~line 282; /scaffold-plan → The neighbour check, ~line 462), while the shipping skill now reads Objective + Scope + Approach.
findings.why_it_matters: The repo's direction is one-way — the spec is the source and skills are derived from it — so the next agent propagating spec→skill removes the `## Approach` read as an undeclared skill invention, and re-breaks seam visibility (the same defect flagged above in audit). The spec is also the only place both readers (plan, audit) are described together; while it says two sections, audit reading two sections looks correct.
findings.fix: Update both ARCHITECTURE passages to `## Objective`, `## Scope` and `## Approach` of every unexecuted sibling, with the one-clause reason (`## Approach` holds the written seam and the owned forward pointer, so without it a resolved overlap re-reports on every re-finalize).

findings.summary: Three places now declare that a phase plan with no `## Phases` entry is "a structural finding for `checkpoint`" (ARCHITECTURE State Determination; scaffold-plan finalize step 2 — "note the missing entry for `/scaffold-checkpoint` to add"; scaffold-audit's plan-set bullet), but checkpoint has no check that detects it and no licence to write it.
findings.why_it_matters: Checkpoint's structural sweep grades "required sections … per the shapes in Step 5", and Step 5 covers only milestone.md, state.md, knowledge, architecture, project and roadmap — it never enumerates `phases/*.md` against `## Phases`. Coherence check 6 only validates the one phase `## Next` names. Step 5a further says "If a *plan* shifted (phases reordered/scope changed), that's `scaffold-plan`'s job — note and route." So plan routes the finding to checkpoint, checkpoint routes plan-shape work back to plan, and the unlisted plan — which the new 'unexecuted = unticked or absent' rule makes load-bearing for the neighbour check and the pivot sweep — is never listed by anyone.
findings.fix: Either give checkpoint the check explicitly (in Step 7's structural list: every `milestones/*/phases/*.md` has an entry in that milestone's `## Phases`; add the missing entry under the repair licence, since 5a already owns that checklist), or — the cheaper fix — make `plan` add the sibling's missing entry itself while it is already in `milestone.md` at finalize, and drop the checkpoint routing sentence from plan, audit and ARCHITECTURE.

findings.summary: Plan-set coherence is now both a `contracts/phase-plan.md` Rule ("No two unexecuted plans in a milestone claim the same deliverable") and a Step 3 reality-pass bullet, so audit grades it twice under two different bars.
findings.why_it_matters: Step 2 instructs the grading subagent to walk the contract's Rules line by line and "emit an explicit verdict — pass / fail / n-a" for each, per doc. That grader sees the contract's subtraction test but not the Step 3 admission bar (name the one artifact; the forward-pointer route with its owner exemption), and it grades one plan at a time, so it cannot see the siblings the rule is about. Result: either a duplicate finding reported twice with two bars, or a fabricated 'fail' on a doc the grader could not evaluate — in a change whose whole premise is that a second home is the disease. The same double-home applies to the contract's `## Governed by` rules (mandatory / empty-is-malformed / verbatim sentence), which need no code and are graded in both Step 2 and Step 3.
findings.fix: State the split explicitly: Step 2's per-rule walk marks the cross-plan rule `n-a` (it is a milestone-level, multi-doc grade) and the doc-local `## Governed by` rules are graded there and NOT restated in Step 3 — leave Step 3 only what needs disk/code (path resolution, sha ancestry, pasted-rule detection, the cross-plan comparison). Add a line to Step 2 saying which contract rules are deliberately deferred to Step 3, so the grader does not treat the deferral as a miss.

findings.summary: `## Governed by` is stamped at finalize and nothing re-checks it: a `knowledge/` doc added or rewritten after a plan is finalized never updates, invalidates, or flags that plan's read-set — while its twin `## Targets` has a deterministic freshness gate.
findings.why_it_matters: `integrate` Step 4b places new `knowledge/` docs and `checkpoint` 5c writes them; neither looks at unexecuted plans. `checkpoint`'s coherence check 5 covers plan-vs-*decision* staleness only, and `plan`'s pivot sweep fires only on a pivot. `go`'s freshness check exempts everything under `.scaffold/` by design. So the phase that a brand-new governing rule most obviously binds executes with a read-set that predates the rule, and `go`'s new contradiction stop never fires because the doc is not in the list to be read. The change's stated payoff — plans stop pasting rules because the pointer is honoured — is exactly what makes this hole load-bearing: the rule now exists in only one place, and the plan does not point at it.
findings.fix: Give it one home. Cheapest: extend `checkpoint`'s coherence check 5 from "plan-vs-decision" to "plan-vs-decision-or-knowledge" — when this session added or materially changed a `knowledge/`/`decisions/` doc, flag every unexecuted finalized plan in the active milestone whose `## Governed by` does not name it, and route it (7b route 3) as a re-finalize. Add the reciprocal one-liner to `integrate`'s Step 4b ("a new knowledge doc may bind an already-finalized plan — say so and route to `/scaffold-plan --final`"), and state the obligation in ARCHITECTURE where the read-set is defined.

findings.summary: scaffold-status now defines a no-active-phase fallback for "Coming up" (take the first three unticked entries and say the cursor is lost), but ARCHITECTURE's /scaffold-status section states only "the unticked entries following the active one".
findings.why_it_matters: Minor, but it is skill-invented behaviour in a section the spec describes in full and does not delegate (unlike the neighbour check, where the spec explicitly points at the skill for the procedure). The next spec→skill propagation pass has grounds to delete it, re-opening the hole it was written to close.
findings.fix: Add one clause to ARCHITECTURE's `/scaffold-status` paragraph: when no active phase resolves (`## Next` silent or dangling), it names the first three unticked entries and says the cursor is unanchored.

findings.summary: The "more than three hits" hard stop never says what one hit is — per scope item, per sibling plan, or per (item × sibling) pair — so the same overlap set can compute as 2 hits or 6 and either complete or abort the finalize.
findings.why_it_matters: A cold agent finalizing phase 09 against three unexecuted siblings, where two siblings each partly duplicate two of its four scope items, has to choose a counting unit with no rule to apply. Count by item → 2 hits, resolve them, finalize completes. Count by pair → 4 hits, which triggers the hard stop: the plan stays a draft, `state.md` `## Next` keeps pointing at an unfinalized plan, and `go` refuses. Two agents reading the same instruction on the same milestone produce opposite outcomes on the single branch that halts the skill.
findings.fix: State the unit explicitly in step 2, e.g. after "Zero hits is the normal result": "**One hit = one scope item of this plan**, however many siblings it collides with — the count is items in trouble, not comparisons made." (Then mirror the same sentence in ARCHITECTURE.md's plan-set coherence invariant so the spec carries it.)

findings.summary: The `## Governed by` candidate listing is "every file in `.scaffold/decisions/`" with no instruction to skip a decision whose `Status:` is `Superseded by [[NNNN-…]]`, so a dead ruling can be listed as binding.
findings.why_it_matters: `decisions/` is append-only by design — plan's own Phase 3 says a superseded ADR keeps its file and only flips its `Status:` line. At finalize the candidate listing shows "filenames plus each doc's opening rule/ruling line", which for a superseded ADR is still an assertive ruling; the binding test ("if you built this phase in violation of this rule, would the phase be wrong?") answers yes on its face. `go` then resolves the path, reads the dead ruling in full, and — because the current approach was built on the *superseding* ADR — hits Step 3's "a rule that contradicts `## Approach` stops `go` too" exit: the phase halts, builds nothing, and routes to checkpoint over a ruling that was already replaced.
findings.fix: Add to finalize step 3's candidate rule: "Skip any `decisions/` file whose `Status:` is `Superseded by …` — its ruling is not live; if its successor binds, list the successor. Only `Accepted` ADRs are candidates." Mirror it in go's Step 3 (a listed superseded ADR is a re-finalize finding, not a contradiction) and in audit's `## Governed by` grading.

findings.summary: plan is the only writer of `## Governed by`, yet it is never told that an empty heading is malformed, that the section and the `Governed by: none` sentence are mutually exclusive, or that a re-finalize must delete whichever form no longer applies.
findings.why_it_matters: On a re-finalize where the binding docs have gone away (the knowledge doc graduated into `architecture.md`, or scope narrowed), the instruction reads "on a re-finalize, **replace** the existing section" — replacing a one-entry list with nothing leaves the bare `## Governed by` heading, and the author then writes the none-sentence into `## Approach` as told. Both readers reject the result: `go` Step 3 stops on "`## Governed by` is empty — it names nothing to read", and audit grades it malformed. The finalize seam has already been approved by the user, so the failure surfaces only at execution. The reverse case is unruled too: a plan that previously carried the none-sentence and now has a binding doc keeps the stale sentence, and nothing tells the author to remove it.
findings.fix: In finalize step 3, add: "The two forms are exclusive and a re-finalize must end in exactly one. If nothing binds, **delete the `## Governed by` heading entirely** (an empty heading is malformed — `go` stops on it) and write the fixed sentence into `## Approach`. If something binds, write the section and **delete any `Governed by: none` line** left in `## Approach`."

findings.summary: Audit's plan-set coherence check tells the grader to compare `## Objective` + `## Scope` of unexecuted plans, but every exculpatory signal it must then apply — a written seam, a forward pointer that names an owner — lives in `## Approach`, which its stated comparison set does not include.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the defect already fixed in plan's neighbour check ("those three sections only", `## Approach` added precisely because seams live there) left unfixed in the skill that grades the same rule. A fresh audit subagent handed "compare the `## Objective` + `## Scope`" reads only those two sections, sees phase 08 item 3 and phase 09 item 1 both landing the same migration, and files a finding — while the seam sentence plan wrote into 09's `## Approach` ("08-splits item 6 owns adding the column; this phase assumes it exists") sits one section below, unread. Audit's own instruction warns "grade exactly what `plan`'s neighbour check grades, or you punish conformance"; as written it punishes exactly the plans that followed the prescribed resolution, on every audit run, with no way for the user to make the finding go away.
findings.fix: Change the comparison-set sentence to "compare the `## Objective` + `## Scope` + `## Approach` of its **unexecuted** plans" and add "`## Approach` is in the read set because that is where a written seam and an owned forward pointer live — the two things that make an apparent overlap not a finding."

findings.summary: When the right resolution for a hit is "take the whole item here and drop it from the sibling" but that sibling is finalized-and-unexecuted, the skill forbids the edit and says to "re-finalize it through the normal pass" without saying whether the current finalize completes, halts, or must fall back to a this-plan-only resolution.
findings.why_it_matters: "Every hit resolves before finalize" is absolute, and for a partial hit the only two legal moves are narrow-here or take-whole-and-drop-from-the-sibling. If the agent judges the second is correct and the sibling is finalized, it is simultaneously told the hit must resolve now, that the sibling may not be edited, and that the sibling should be re-finalized later — with no ruling on the plan in hand. One agent finalizes anyway and leaves the duplicate live in the finalized sibling (the work still gets built twice, which is the whole defect); another halts and leaves the user with two unfinalizable plans and a cursor pointing at a draft. The `## Approach` seam sentence does not cover it, since a seam describes a split, not a transfer.
findings.fix: Add the exit to the "Whose file the edit lands in" paragraph: "If the only correct resolution requires editing a **finalized** sibling, do not finalize this plan on a promise — either resolve it with a this-plan-only move (narrow to the remainder, or drop it here) and record the seam in `## Approach`, or stop: report that sibling `NN-slug` must be re-finalized first, leave this plan a draft, and finalize again once it has."

findings.summary: Step 2 invents a fourth verdict, **deferred → Step 3**, but the derived-grade rule three paragraphs later still reads "conforms only if every rule passed", and the contract instructs the opposite token (**n-a**) for the very rule audit names as the deferred example.
findings.why_it_matters: An agent grading a normal finalized phase plan emits `deferred` for at least two rules (the plan-set coherence rule, every `## Governed by` path-resolution rule). Neither is a pass, so by the stated derivation the doc cannot grade `conforms` — every conformant phase plan in the project comes back `minor` or `malformed`, and audit's own hard gate ("a doc malformed enough that its state can't be read") can then fire on clean plans. Simultaneously contracts/phase-plan.md says of the plan-set rule "a per-document conformance grade marks it **n-a**", so the grader is handed two different tokens for one rule and must guess which document governs — with the spec being the source, the skill is the wrong one.
findings.fix: Pick one token. Either (a) delete `deferred` and have cross-doc/disk-evidence rules take **n-a** in Step 2 with a pointer to the Step 3 bullet that owns them (matching the contract), or (b) keep `deferred` and (i) amend the contract's plan-set Rule to say `deferred`, and (ii) amend the derived-grade sentence to "conforms only if every rule passed, was n-a, or was deferred *and* passed its Step 3 check".

findings.summary: The contract's new rule that a `## Governed by` decisions entry must name an ADR whose `**Status:**` is `Accepted` (and its matching anti-pattern) can only be graded by opening the other document, so it takes the new `deferred → Step 3` verdict — but Step 3's `## Governed by` bullet checks path resolution, folder scope, wikilink shape and pasted rules, and never checks ADR status.
findings.why_it_matters: The one governance defect the contract calls out as dangerous in its own words — "`go` reads a dead ruling as binding law", and a plan finalized before the supersession stays *final & fresh* because `.scaffold/` is exempt from the freshness test — is now deferred by Step 2 into a Step 3 that has no receiving check. It is graded by nobody: audit reports clean, `go` resolves the path fine and executes under a Superseded ADR. The deferral wording ("each rule is graded once, where its evidence is") makes an agent confident the check happened elsewhere.
findings.fix: Add to Step 3's `## Governed by` bullet: for every entry under `.scaffold/decisions/`, open the ADR and read its `**Status:**` line; anything other than `Accepted` is a finding — `Superseded by [[NNNN-…]]` routes to `plan` to repoint at the successor, `Proposed` routes to the ADR gate. Then the deferral has a landing place.

findings.summary: Both hard stops ("more than three hits" and "the only correct resolution needs a finalized sibling") say "finalize does not complete, the plan stays a draft" — but step 5's mandated re-run of the subtraction test happens *after* step 4 has written and stamped `## Targets`, and nothing tells the agent to remove it, so "stays a draft" is false on disk.
findings.why_it_matters: A hard stop triggered by a re-run hit at step 5 leaves the file carrying `## Governed by` and `_as of <sha>_`. `go`'s state test is content-derived: `## Targets` present + stamp an ancestor of HEAD + nothing undeclared moved = **final & fresh**, and `.scaffold/` edits are exempt from that test. The next `go` therefore executes a plan whose overlap was never resolved — the exact duplicate build this whole change exists to stop — while `state.md`'s cursor still points at it. The same hole applies to a *re*-finalize of an already-finalized plan: entering finalize the file already has `## Targets`, so any hard stop at step 2 leaves it executable too.
findings.fix: State the demotion explicitly at both hard stops: "delete `## Targets` (and the `## Governed by` section written this pass) before stopping — a plan that stays a draft must read as one on disk, per *A rewritten plan is not a fresh plan*", and say the cursor must not be advanced. Alternatively move the `## Targets` write to the last step, after the step 5 re-run, so no stop can leave a stamp behind.

findings.summary: The `/scaffold-plan` finalize-pass bullet describes the order as "writes `## Targets` (stamped `as of HEAD`), **writes `## Governed by`** …, **runs the neighbour check** (below), tightens Scope/Approach", while the shipping skill numbers them neighbour check (2) → Governed by (3) → Targets (4) → tighten (5), and frames the neighbour check as running "before you commit to a scope".
findings.why_it_matters: The spec is the source and skills are derived from it, so the next person propagating from ARCHITECTURE re-derives a sequence that stamps `## Targets` before the check that can abort the finalize — which is precisely the residue-on-disk failure above. It also contradicts the skill's own stated reason for running the check first (the scope must not be committed to before the check).
findings.fix: Reorder the ARCHITECTURE bullet to match the skill: researches the current code, runs the neighbour check, writes `## Governed by`, writes `## Targets` (stamped `as of HEAD`), tightens Scope/Approach, stranger test, presents.

findings.summary: The Execution-model / `/scaffold-plan` passage resolves the finalized-sibling case with "a **finalized** sibling never in place — it was stamped against code, so editing it silently changes what `go` builds; it re-finalizes instead", implying the current finalize proceeds; the skill now rules the opposite — a hard stop, this plan stays a draft, and "never re-finalize a sibling from inside this pass".
findings.why_it_matters: Two documents now answer the same question differently, and the reader has no rule for which governs — the exact defect class this change was written to remove. Worse, ARCHITECTURE's phrasing ("it re-finalizes") reads as a licence to re-finalize the sibling inline, which the skill forbids because the sibling's own neighbour check would then read this plan's pre-edit scope off disk.
findings.fix: Rewrite the ARCHITECTURE sentence to state the skill's rule: a finalized sibling is never edited in place; prefer a this-plan-only move (narrow to the remainder, or drop here on a whole hit); if none is correct, finalize hard-stops, the plan stays a draft, and the sibling is re-finalized in a separate pass first.

findings.summary: Step 4 now justifies placement with "(the contract fixes the section order: Acceptance, Governed by, Targets, and `/scaffold-audit` grades it)", but `grep -n -i order contracts/phase-plan.md skills/scaffold-audit/SKILL.md` returns nothing — the contract states order only implicitly in its template block, has no Rule or Anti-pattern about order, and audit has no order check.
findings.why_it_matters: This is the previously-found false citation ("checkpoint's sweep checks order") re-pointed at a different skill rather than removed, so a MANDATORY placement is still enforced by nothing: a plan that puts `## Governed by` after `## Targets`, or between Scope and Approach, passes audit's per-rule walk (every Rule and Anti-pattern is checked by name, and none mentions order) and passes checkpoint. Every reader downstream that greps by section still works, so the drift is silent — and the citation makes a future editor believe a grader exists.
findings.fix: Either add a Rule to contracts/phase-plan.md ("Sections appear in the order of the Required-structure template: Objective, Scope, Approach, Acceptance, Governed by, Targets; a section out of order is malformed") so audit's Step 2 walk actually grades it, or drop the parenthetical claim from the skill and state the placement as a convention with no grader.

findings.summary: The new passage says "Any finalized plan whose read-set doesn't name this doc's path is named in the Step 6 report and routed: 'run `/scaffold-plan --final` on it'" — the trigger is the *absence of the path*, with no test for whether the new doc's rule actually binds that phase.
findings.why_it_matters: Every unexecuted finalized plan fails that condition for every newly placed knowledge doc, by construction — a doc just created is in no plan's read-set. So integrating one doc routes the entire finalized queue back through finalize, each of which re-stamps `## Targets`, re-runs the neighbour check and re-consumes the approval seam. An agent following it literally produces a mass re-finalize; an agent that senses the absurdity has to invent a relevance test, which is the guess this change exists to eliminate. Note that `plan` has the test already and states it positively; integrate omits it. The reach is also narrower than the defect: only the *active* milestone is read, while audit's plan-set pass walks "each live milestone", and a placed `decisions/` ADR gets no equivalent sweep at all.
findings.fix: Give integrate `plan`'s binding test verbatim: for each unexecuted finalized plan, ask "if this phase were built in violation of this document's rule, would the phase be wrong?" — route only the plans that answer yes, and say plainly that a plan the new doc does not bind is not a finding. Widen "the active milestone" to every live milestone, or state explicitly why the active one is the only reach.

findings.summary: ARCHITECTURE's `/scaffold-status` passage defines the window as "up to three, in list order, taken from the unticked entries following the active one", with a no-active-phase fallback — the shipping skill now additionally hoists unticked entries that sit *before* the active one ("stranded, not gone — name it first, marked stranded, inside the same three").
findings.why_it_matters: The fix to the stranded-window defect landed in the derived artifact only, so the spec now positively states the rule the skill was changed to stop doing ("following the active one"). Anyone propagating from the source — the direction this repo mandates — reinstates the blind spot, and `/scaffold-audit`'s spec-vs-skill drift check has two documents to choose between with no tiebreak.
findings.fix: Update the ARCHITECTURE paragraph to carry the skill's rule: up to three unticked entries, stranded ones (unticked and positioned before the active entry) named first and marked stranded, the remainder taken in list order after the active one; keep the cursor-lost fallback as written.

findings.summary: New structural check 4 tells checkpoint to "add the unticked entry in list position" for any plan file with no `## Phases` entry, unconditionally — there is no branch for a plan file whose work was actually built in an earlier session and simply never listed, and no rule for deciding the list position beyond "in list position".
findings.why_it_matters: The unlisted-plan case arises mostly from a session that ended without a checkpoint — i.e. exactly the case where the phase may have been executed. Writing it unticked asserts on disk that done work is undone, and unexecuted is now a load-bearing set: the plan enters `plan`'s neighbour check reach, where a subtraction hit against it can legally cause a live plan to **drop** an item to "the sibling that owns it" — a sibling that will never run. It also enters the pivot sweep and audit's plan-set pass. The check's own justification ("listing a file that exists decides nothing") is false for precisely this case: the tick state is a decision.
findings.fix: Split the branch: if the plan carries `## Targets` and its targets show as built (or the session record shows it ran), ask before writing — checkpoint's route-2 ask — rather than defaulting to unticked; state the default position rule explicitly (by the plan's `NN-` filename prefix), and say that an entry whose executed state is unclear is route 2, not fix-on-sight.

findings.summary: The new bullet sends a governing-rule-vs-`## Approach` contradiction down the existing "not satisfiable as written" exit and to `/scaffold-checkpoint` — but that exit's stated remedy is that "`/scaffold-checkpoint` records it (it abandons the phase, which clears the cursor)", which is the wrong disposition for this contradiction and is never corrected.
findings.why_it_matters: A phase whose approach collides with a `knowledge/` rule is not an unbuildable phase; it needs the approach re-decided under the rule, which the skill itself says is `plan`'s call. Following the text literally, the agent tells the user to checkpoint, checkpoint abandons the phase and clears the cursor, and a scoped, approved, still-necessary phase is deleted from the queue with the reconciliation nobody performed. Nothing in the new text names `/scaffold-plan --final` as the return path, and checkpoint has no branch that distinguishes this class of abandonment.
findings.fix: Have the bullet name its own disposition rather than borrowing the exit's: report the rule, its path and the conflicting approach step, build nothing, and route to `/scaffold-plan --final` to re-decide the approach under the rule — with `/scaffold-checkpoint` first only to record the stop, explicitly *not* to abandon the phase.

findings.summary: Integrate's new read-set staleness flag classifies any plan with no `## Governed by` section as a draft, but the contract makes a *finalized* plan governed by nothing carry the verbatim `Governed by: none` sentence and **no section at all** — so the finalized plans that asserted "nothing governs me" are exactly the ones the flag silently skips.
findings.why_it_matters: A phase plan finalized with the `Governed by: none` line, then a `knowledge/` doc placed by `/scaffold-integrate` that now binds it: integrate reads the plan, sees no `## Governed by` section, concludes "a plan without one is a draft — it needs no flag", and reports nothing. `go` later executes that plan under a rule it never read, and no other defense covers it (the freshness gate exempts everything under `.scaffold/`). The check therefore misses precisely the class it was added for.
findings.fix: In the Step 4b paragraph, replace the draft test with the contract's actual state test: a plan is finalized iff it carries `## Targets` (state derivation is `## Targets`, per contracts/phase-plan.md "Draft vs. final"). Then: a finalized plan whose `## Governed by` doesn't name the placed doc's path — **including one carrying the `Governed by: none` sentence and no section** — is flagged and routed to `/scaffold-plan --final`; a plan with no `## Targets` is the draft that needs no flag.

findings.summary: `/scaffold-integrate` now performs a read-set staleness check over unexecuted phase plans (SKILL.md line 120), but ARCHITECTURE's `/scaffold-integrate` section (line 604) says only "Absorbs a spec or doc… Does not execute work, author phase plans", and the Skill × Artifact table (line 689) gives integrate `—` on `…/phases/NN-slug.md` — no access at all, not even read.
findings.why_it_matters: The repo's direction rule is one-way: the spec is the source and skills are derived. An agent regenerating scaffold-integrate from ARCHITECTURE would not build this check at all, and an agent auditing skills against the coverage table would read the phase-plan `—` as proof integrate must not touch plans and delete the passage. The only defense that catches "a knowledge doc landed after a plan was finalized" would vanish with it.
findings.fix: Add the behaviour to ARCHITECTURE: in the `/scaffold-integrate` section, state that after placing a `knowledge/` doc integrate reads the `## Governed by` of every unexecuted plan in the active milestone and routes any finalized plan whose read-set predates it to `/scaffold-plan --final` (it never edits a plan); and change the phase-plan row's integrate cell from `—` to `R (flag read-set predating a placed knowledge doc)`. Reference it from the Execution model's `## Governed by` bullet as the read-set's staleness defense.

findings.summary: Audit's Step 2 tells the grader to give the plan-set coherence rule (and a `## Governed by` path resolving on disk) the verdict **deferred → Step 3**, while contracts/phase-plan.md twice prescribes the verdict **n-a** for a per-document conformance pass ("a per-document conformance grade marks it **n-a**"; "n-a for a per-document conformance pass").
findings.why_it_matters: The two verdict tokens are not interchangeable in audit's own grade arithmetic: "A doc's overall grade … **conforms only if every rule passed**" (line 89). `n-a` is explicitly a non-blocking token elsewhere in the skill; `deferred` is not in that set, so every phase plan carrying a `## Governed by` path acquires at least one non-passing verdict and can never be graded *conforms* — and audit's conformance pass gates the reality pass, so a whole tree of correct plans reports as not-conforming.
findings.fix: Make the skill match the contract: mark cross-document / code-evidence rules **n-a** in the Step 2 per-rule table (n-a is already the token for "this contract rule doesn't apply to this file alone"), and say the substantive check happens in Step 3 — e.g. "verdict **n-a (graded in Step 3)**". Alternatively add `deferred` to the derived-grade sentence as non-blocking, but the contract's word is `n-a`, so change the skill, not the contract.

findings.summary: `status` derives the plan state from `## Targets` alone (Step 4 "Plan state?", Step 6 routing) and never looks at `## Governed by`, so it reports a finalized plan carrying neither the section nor the `Governed by: none` line as **final & fresh** and tells the user to run `/scaffold-go` — the plan the contract calls malformed and `go` refuses at Step 3.
findings.why_it_matters: The session-entry briefing routes the user straight into a refusal: status says "final & fresh … Run /scaffold-go to execute it", `go` loads the plan, passes the freshness gate, then stops with "This plan carries no `## Governed by` and no `Governed by: none` line". Status's own health check (Step 5 item 9) enumerates exactly this class of cross-doc contradiction and omits this one, even though the test is a single grep on a file status has already opened.
findings.fix: Add a health-check bullet (Step 5 item 9) and a note on the Step 4 plan-state computation: a plan carrying `## Targets` but neither a non-empty `## Governed by` nor the verbatim line `Governed by: none — no `knowledge/` or `decisions/` document constrains this phase.` in `## Approach` is **malformed, not runnable** — report it as such and route to `/scaffold-plan --final` instead of offering `/scaffold-go`.

findings.summary: ARCHITECTURE's `/scaffold-go` section (line 506ff) states only that `go` reads every document `## Governed by` names and that "a path that does not resolve stops `go`" — it omits the three other read-set behaviours the shipping skill now carries: an **empty** `## Governed by` stops `go`, **neither section nor verbatim sentence** stops `go`, and a governing rule that **contradicts `## Approach`** takes the *not-satisfiable-as-written* exit.
findings.why_it_matters: Spec and skill disagreeing means the skill is wrong unless the spec is; here the skill is right and the source has rotted — the same defect already fixed once for the neighbour check. A regeneration or a spec-vs-skill audit pass would strip `go`'s empty-section stop and its contradiction exit, and the contradiction exit is the one that keeps `go` from silently choosing between an approved approach and a binding rule (a decision the spec says is `plan`'s).
findings.fix: Extend the `final & fresh` bullet in ARCHITECTURE's `/scaffold-go` section: `go` stops on a dangling path, on an empty `## Governed by`, and on a finalized plan carrying neither the section nor the contract's verbatim `Governed by: none` line; and a document named in the read-set that forbids what `## Approach` directs routes to the **unsatisfiable exit** (`go` never picks between them — that is `plan`'s decision).

findings.summary: ARCHITECTURE's `/scaffold-status` section (line ~432) still defines "Coming up" as "the unticked entries **following** the active one", while the shipping skill now names an unticked entry that sits *before* the active one first, marked **stranded**, inside the same three.
findings.why_it_matters: The cursor-lost fallback from the same round was propagated into ARCHITECTURE but the stranded rule was not, so the spec now contradicts the skill on which entries the window contains. A regeneration from the spec re-introduces the window that hides a stranded phase — the entry most likely to be the duplicated or stale one, and the reason the stranded rule was added.
findings.fix: In the "Names what is coming, not just what is active" paragraph, state that the window is the milestone's unticked entries with an entry *before* the cursor named first and marked stranded (it is unexecuted by the same rule the neighbour check and audit's plan-set check walk — unticked or absent), still capped at three.

findings.summary: The three statements of who enforces plan-set coherence disagree: contracts/phase-plan.md says it is "checked by `scaffold-plan`'s neighbour check at finalize **and by `/scaffold-audit`'s reality pass**", audit implements it (Step 3, "Plan-set coherence within a milestone"), but ARCHITECTURE's Execution model bullet (line 273) names only `plan`'s neighbour check — and scaffold-checkpoint argues "a second home for it here would be exactly the duplication the one-home rule forbids".
findings.why_it_matters: Read together, ARCHITECTURE (the authority) plus checkpoint's one-home argument make audit's plan-set check look like an illegal second home, and this repo's own rules say the spec wins — so a coherence pass would delete it. Audit's is the only check that can see an overlap between two plans when neither is being finalized (a pre-written predetermined milestone, or two plans finalized before the check existed); removing it leaves that case defended by nothing.
findings.fix: In the Execution model → Plan-set coherence bullet, state both enforcers, as the contract does: `plan`'s neighbour check at finalize (author-time, resolves) and `/scaffold-audit`'s reality pass (after-the-fact, reports, routes to `plan`) — and say why two homes are not duplication here (one writes at authoring, one grades read-only across the set). Then soften checkpoint's line to "the disposal of this belongs to `plan` at finalize and `audit` on demand — checkpoint is not a third grader."

findings.summary: Status's "Coming up" cites the shared unexecuted rule — "unticked **or absent**", the same rule `plan`'s neighbour check and `audit`'s plan-set check walk — but computes the list purely from `milestone.md`'s `## Phases` entries, so a plan file in `phases/` with no checklist entry never appears.
findings.why_it_matters: A just-authored sibling with no checklist entry is in reach of the neighbour check and of audit's coherence check, and it is the highest-risk overlap candidate — yet the one surface that exists so the user "can spot an overlap or a mis-ordered cut" cannot show it. Status also has no health-check line for an unlisted plan file, so on a cold resume the user sees neither the plan nor the structural gap (only the next `checkpoint` will).
findings.fix: Either narrow the claim (drop "or absent" from the stranded rationale, since status computes off entries only) or implement it: one `ls .scaffold/milestones/<active>/phases/` and name any plan file with no `## Phases` entry in "Coming up", marked *unlisted*, plus a health-check bullet "a plan file with no `## Phases` entry — `/scaffold-checkpoint` adds it (structural check 4)".
