findings.summary: Status still derives "final & fresh → ready to `go`" from `## Targets` alone, but `go` now refuses any finalized plan that lacks a non-empty `## Governed by` or the verbatim `Governed by: none` line — so status routes the user straight into a refusal it never anticipated.
findings.why_it_matters: Every phase plan finalized before this change has `## Targets` and no `## Governed by`. A stranger runs `/scaffold-status` on such a repo, Step 4 computes the stamp as holding, Step 5 item 2 reports "final & fresh", Step 6 prints "Run `/scaffold-go` to execute it" — and `go` Step 3 immediately stops with "This plan carries no `## Governed by` and no `Governed by: none` line". Status is the session-entry skill; it is precisely the place the user learns whether they can execute, and it gives the wrong answer on the entire installed base of pre-existing plans. Nothing in status mentions the read-set at all.
findings.fix: In Step 4's "Plan state?" bullet, add the read-set to the final-plan test: a plan with `## Targets` whose `## Governed by` is absent-and-with-no-verbatim-`Governed by: none`-line in `## Approach`, is empty, or names a path that doesn't resolve, reports as **final, read-set malformed — re-finalize before `go`**, not as final & fresh. Mirror it in Step 6's routing block as a fourth branch, and add a Step 5 item 9 health-check line for the dangling-path case. The plan file is already open at Step 2, so this costs one grep plus one existence check per listed path.

findings.summary: Step 4's "What's coming?" bullet asserts its window is unexecuted "by the same rule `plan`'s neighbour check and `audit`'s plan-set check walk (unticked **or absent**)", but its stated computation reads only entries in `## Phases` and forbids extra reads — a plan file with no `## Phases` entry can never appear.
findings.why_it_matters: An agent following this cannot proceed without guessing. The bullet ends "Already-open file, no extra reads", so a plan file sitting in `phases/` that was never added to the checklist is structurally invisible to "Coming up" — yet the same paragraph tells the reader it is in the window and, worse, that such a plan is *more* likely to be the duplicated one. A stranger either (a) obeys the no-extra-reads instruction and silently omits exactly the plan the parenthetical singles out as high-risk, or (b) lists `phases/` and reads plan titles, contradicting the stated cost model and the read-only-cheap framing. Both readings are defensible from the text, which is the defect. The claimed unlisted-plan case is also the one `plan`'s neighbour check and `audit` both go out of their way to cover, so status is the only one of the three that quietly drops it.
findings.fix: Pick one and state it. Either drop "or absent" from the parenthetical and say plainly that status lists checklist entries only, noting that an unlisted plan file is `checkpoint`/`audit`'s to catch; or add one directory listing of the active milestone's `phases/` and define the ordering rule for a plan file with no `## Phases` entry (e.g. list it last inside the same three, marked *unlisted*) — and drop the "no extra reads" claim.

findings.summary: "Auto-finalize when next up" sits at the end of Phase 5, so on a pivot the new plan is finalized — neighbour check and all — before Phase 6's stale-plan sweep rewrites the very sibling plans that check was run against, and the sweep can then demote the plan just finalized.
findings.why_it_matters: Inserting phases into the active milestone *is* a pivot by Phase 6's own definition ("phases reordered/replaced/**inserted**"), and authoring-then-auto-finalizing an inserted phase is the canonical path through this skill. So the common case is: Phase 5 authors 09.1, auto-finalize runs the neighbour check against siblings 10 and 11 as they read on disk and stamps `## Targets`; Phase 6 then re-reads 10 and 11 against the same change and "flags and rewrites in place" — new scope, new deliverables — and the neighbour check's verdict is now against text that no longer exists. Phase 6 also sweeps "every unexecuted plan in the active milestone", which includes the plan just finalized, and step 2 there says rewriting a finalized plan demotes it to draft and deletes its `## Targets`. A stranger following the file in order finalizes a plan and then, three sections later, is told to consider demoting it — with nothing saying whether to re-finalize, whether the neighbour check must re-run, or whether to have deferred the auto-finalize at all.
findings.fix: Move the auto-finalize offer out of Phase 5 to after Phase 6, or gate it: "If the direction is a pivot, run Phase 6's sweep first — the sweep may rewrite the siblings this plan's neighbour check reads, and a plan finalized before it can be demoted by it. Offer auto-finalize only once the sweep is complete." Add one line to Phase 6 excluding the plan authored in this invocation from demotion, or requiring a re-finalize if the sweep touches it.

findings.summary: No shipping skill shows a single example `## Governed by` line, and the author's rule ("repo-relative paths, one per line, each with a few words naming which rule binds") and the grader's rule ("every entry is a repo-relative path … an entry written as a `[[wikilink]]`, a doc title, or **prose** is malformed") can be read as contradicting each other on whether the mandated note is allowed on the line.
findings.why_it_matters: Every other machine-read construct in this change ships with its literal form: the stamp is spelled `_as of <sha>_`, the escape hatch is a verbatim sentence, `## Targets` explains trailing-`/` matching. The read-set — a section that `go` must parse into paths and stop hard on — ships with none. A stranger authoring it guesses the shape (bullet? bare line? path first or last? backticked?), and a stranger grading it in `audit` reads "an entry … written as … prose is malformed" and can fail a conformant `- \`.scaffold/knowledge/tenancy.md\` — every query filters by org_id` line, since half the entry *is* prose. `go`'s wording ("each a repo-relative path with a note naming which rule") is a third phrasing. This is a false-malformed finding on correctly authored plans, routed back to a re-finalize that will produce the identical text.
findings.fix:
Add one literal exemplar to `scaffold-plan` finalize step 3 and quote the same line in `scaffold-audit`'s `## Governed by` bullet, e.g.:

```
## Governed by
- `.scaffold/knowledge/tenancy.md` — every query filters by `org_id`
- `.scaffold/decisions/0007-single-writer.md` — one writer per aggregate
```

and in audit reword the malformed test to "the entry's **path token** is a repo-relative path; the trailing note naming the rule is required and is never itself a finding."

findings.summary: The neighbour check's second admission route (an unresolved forward pointer) produces a hit that fits none of the legal resolutions and none of the counting rule, because both are keyed exclusively to the subtraction test's answer.
findings.why_it_matters: An agent finalizing a plan whose sibling's ## Approach says "a decision for the audit" has, by the text, a hit that "resolves before finalize". It then reads "**which resolutions are legal depends on which answer produced it**" and finds three bullets keyed to "No, not at all" / "Only partly" / "both genuinely touch the work" — a pointer hit produced no such answer, so no resolution is licensed. It also reads "**One hit = one scope item of this plan**", but a pointer in the sibling's prose may attach to no scope item of this plan at all, so the hit is uncountable against the >3 hard stop. Both the mandatory resolution and the mandatory count become guesses — the exact defect class (an instruction obeyed correctly and still incomplete) this change exists to kill. Audit repeats the same two routes but only reports, so nothing downstream compensates.
findings.fix: In finalize step 2, give route 2 its own resolution and count: a forward-pointer hit resolves by writing the owner into this plan's `## Approach` ("NN-slug item N owns X; this phase assumes it exists") — which converts it into a written seam, silent forever after — and never by deleting the pointer; and state that a pointer hit counts as one hit whether or not it maps to a scope item, or is explicitly excluded from the >3 count. Mirror the same sentence into ARCHITECTURE's Execution model → Plan-set coherence, which has the identical gap.

findings.summary: A plan carrying BOTH a populated `## Governed by` section and the verbatim `Governed by: none` line is self-contradictory, and only scaffold-plan's prose forbids it — the contract, audit, go and status all pass it.
findings.why_it_matters: The re-finalize path is exactly how it arises: plan's step 3 tells the author "If something binds now and the plan carried the sentence, write the section and **delete** the `Governed by: none` line" — a mandatory deletion enforced by nothing. Forget it and the plan asserts on disk that no knowledge/ or decisions/ document constrains the phase while its own read-set names two. Every reader passes it: the contract's rule is "either the section or the sentence"; audit greps for the section-or-line; `go` sees the section, reads it, proceeds and never looks at the sentence; `status`'s new read-set check is "non-empty `## Governed by` **or** … this line verbatim". A future reader (a stranger-test builder, integrate deciding whether a doc binds, a human) reads the false sentence and concludes nothing governs the phase. The whole point of fixing the wording was to make this computable — the one state that needs the grep is the one nobody greps for.
findings.fix: Add a contract Rule and Anti-pattern: "The two forms are exclusive — a plan carries the `## Governed by` section or the `Governed by: none` line, never both; both present is malformed." Then have audit's Step 2 walk grade it (it is doc-local and a pure grep), `go` stop on it alongside the empty-section case, and `status`'s read-set check report it as malformed.

findings.summary: Finalize step 3 tells the author to skip any `decisions/` file whose Status is not `Accepted`, including a `Proposed` ADR that binds — where the contract requires the ADR gate to resolve first.
findings.why_it_matters: contracts/phase-plan.md says of a candidate: "`Proposed` → the ADR gate resolves first (a plan is never authored on a not-yet-approved ADR), never a pointer", and plan's own Ordering rule says the same. Step 3 instead says only "a `Proposed` one is not law yet" and directs a silent skip, giving no branch for the case where that Proposed ADR is precisely what governs the phase. An agent following step 3 literally finalizes a plan that depends on an unratified decision, writes a `## Governed by` that omits it (or the `Governed by: none` sentence outright), and the omission is then invisible to every downstream check: audit only grades the entries that are listed, and `go` reads only what the list names. Spec and skill disagree, and the skill is the wrong one.
findings.fix: In step 3, split the two non-Accepted cases: `Superseded` → point at the successor if it binds (as written today); `Proposed` → if it would bind, stop and resolve the ADR gate (Phase 3) before finalize completes — never skip it silently. Add the superseded/proposed candidate handling to ARCHITECTURE's finalize-pass bullet so the spec states it too.

findings.summary: The new "a rule that contradicts `## Approach` stops `go`" branch gives no test for what counts as a contradiction — the one mandatory judgement in a skill built as a thin deterministic executor.
findings.why_it_matters: Every sibling check in this change is fenced with an explicit bar and an explicit default (the subtraction test, "Yes → not a finding", "zero hits is the normal result", "the bar is the design", "a gate you pass without reading is not a gate"). This branch has neither. `go` now reads every governing document in full at the start of every session and must decide, per rule, whether it "forbids or rules out what the approach directs" — with no rule for the common shapes: a rule that constrains *how* rather than forbids; a rule the approach simply does not address; a rule that contradicts `## Scope` or a `## Targets` entry rather than `## Approach` (the text names only Approach, so an agent finding a rule that forbids touching a target file has no branch); tension the approach already anticipates in prose. Under-fire and the section's stated purpose ("this is the case the read-set exists to catch") is dead; over-fire and `go` halts approved work on a soft reading — and the stop is expensive, because it costs a full re-finalize.
findings.fix: Give the branch a bar and a default, in `go`'s Step 3: it fires only when the rule and a *named* `## Approach` step (or scope item / target) cannot both hold — you can state the step and the rule and say which would have to be violated to satisfy the other; anything short of that (a rule the approach does not reach, a rule about how rather than whether) is not a contradiction, proceed and execute under the rule. Extend it to `## Scope`/`## Targets` explicitly, and mirror the bar into ARCHITECTURE's `/scaffold-go` section.

findings.summary: The `## Governed by` reality bullet says the doc-local rules "are graded in the Step 2 per-rule walk and are not re-reported here", then restates each of them in imperative finding language, so the grader cannot tell which of them it is supposed to report.
findings.why_it_matters: Right after the disclaimer the bullet says an empty heading "is malformed", a paraphrase of the fixed line "is malformed, and so is neither", an entry as a `[[wikilink]]` or prose "is malformed", a path outside the two folders "is a finding too" — and folder scope needs no disk at all, so it is doc-local by the bullet's own division ("what it adds is the part that needs disk: paths, folder scope, pasted rules" itself contradicts the split). A fresh Step 3 subagent, dispatched without the Step 2 table in hand, follows the imperatives and reports every one of them a second time; a different subagent honours the disclaimer and reports none, including the ones only it can see. The audit report's finding count for a malformed plan is then non-deterministic — in a system whose whole premise is that state is computed the same way twice.
findings.fix: Reduce the restated material to a non-imperative description ("the shape you are resolving: a section with at least one entry, or the fixed line") and keep exactly one imperative list in the bullet — the disk-dependent checks: path resolves, ADR `**Status:**` is `Accepted`, pasted rule. Move folder scope explicitly to Step 2 (it is a pure text test) and say so.

findings.summary: Step 2's new "n-a (graded in Step 3)" verdict defers a rule to a pass that may decline to grade it, and n-a counts toward conformance — so a deferred rule can be graded nowhere and still read as a pass.
findings.why_it_matters: Step 2 defers plan-set coherence and `## Governed by` path resolution as **n-a (graded in Step 3)**, and the derived grade is now "conforms only if every rule passed **or was n-a**". Step 3 is "gated by conformance" and carries a hard gate: "if a doc is malformed enough that its state can't be read reliably … report the reality of that area as **unreliable — fix conformance first**". So a phase plan that fails one doc-local rule (an unparseable checklist in its `milestone.md`, an empty `## Governed by`) hands its deferred rules to a pass that is instructed not to grade them — and the deferral leaves no trace in the derived grade, because n-a is a pass. The dangling read-set path and the duplicated deliverable are then reported by nobody, which is the same silent-hole shape the deferral was introduced to close.
findings.fix: Make the deferral accountable: state that an n-a (graded in Step 3) rule must appear in the Step 4 report with its Step 3 outcome, and that a rule deferred to Step 3 which Step 3 could not grade (the hard gate fired) is reported as **ungraded — blocked by conformance**, naming the malformed doc, and does not count toward "conforms".

findings.summary: The contradiction stop's canned line asserts "Nothing built." unconditionally, but Step 3 also runs when `go` resumes a phase whose earlier deliverables are already on disk.
findings.why_it_matters: The most likely way a governing rule starts contradicting an approved approach is `integrate` placing a `knowledge/` doc mid-phase — i.e. between `go` sessions, after some scope items were built under the now-contradicted approach. On resume, `go` prints "Nothing built." and the user takes the tree to be clean; the re-finalize that follows then re-decides the approach with no one aware that code written under the old one is sitting in the working tree.
findings.fix: Make the line conditional: "Nothing built this session" plus, when scope items are already done, name them — "items 1–N were built under the previous approach; re-finalize decides what happens to them."

findings.summary: The spec and the shipping skill now prescribe opposite dispositions for a governing rule that contradicts `## Approach`: ARCHITECTURE (~line 541) sends it to the **unsatisfiable exit**, whose stated remedy is `checkpoint` **abandoning** the phase (unticked, cursor cleared); skills/scaffold-go/SKILL.md (Step 3, ~line 121-131) says in bold that this is **not** that exit — the scope still holds, the phase is still wanted, only the approach is re-decided, and the cursor stays on the plan.
findings.why_it_matters: A plan whose `knowledge/` rule forbids one approach step ends in two different repo states depending on which document the agent read: `go` following the skill stops and keeps the cursor for a `/scaffold-plan --final` re-decide; `go` regenerated from the spec (the declared one-way direction) hands the phase to `checkpoint` for abandonment, unticking a phase nobody decided to drop and clearing the cursor. The earlier fix landed in the skill only and left the master rotted against it.
findings.fix: In ARCHITECTURE's `/scaffold-go` read-set passage, replace "takes the **unsatisfiable exit** (below)" with the skill's rule: `go` names the rule, its path and the conflicting `## Approach` step, builds nothing further, stops, and routes to `/scaffold-plan --final` — the phase is not abandoned and the cursor stays on the plan; add one clause to the *unsatisfiable exit* paragraph saying the read-set contradiction is explicitly not one of its two exits.

findings.summary: ARCHITECTURE's `/scaffold-integrate` passage (~line 634-640) states the read-set staleness check as "reads the `## Governed by` of every unexecuted plan in the **active milestone** and routes any finalized plan whose read-set **predates the doc**", while skills/scaffold-integrate/SKILL.md line 120 walks "every unexecuted phase plan in every **live** milestone" and routes only on a positive binding test ("if that phase were built in violation of this document's rule, would the phase be wrong?"), stating explicitly that "the absence of the path on its own is never the trigger".
findings.why_it_matters: The spec is the source skills are derived from, so both divergences are live regressions waiting to be re-propagated: the narrower reach silently drops plans in other live milestones that the shipping skill covers, and the absence-based trigger is the exact defect already fixed in the skill — it routes every finalized plan in the repo to `/scaffold-plan --final` after any `knowledge/` placement, which is the rubber-stamp failure the whole design writes against.
findings.fix: Rewrite the ARCHITECTURE integrate bullet to match the skill: reach is every unexecuted plan in every live milestone (never `milestones/archived/`), and the trigger is the binding test plus the absent path — absence alone is not a finding; note that a finalized plan carrying the `Governed by: none` sentence and no section is still in scope.

findings.summary: skills/scaffold-status/SKILL.md now performs a read-set validity check (Step 4 "Read-set intact?", lines 85-93) and reports a fourth plan state — "final, but its read-set is malformed", which takes precedence over *final & fresh* (Step 5 item 2, Step 6 routing lines 173-178) — but ARCHITECTURE says none of it: the `/scaffold-status` section (~line 431-452) mentions only truth docs, `glossary.md` and the coming-up list; State Determination's `Plan state` row still enumerates exactly three states and ends "`go` executes only final & fresh"; and the Skill × Artifact row for `…/phases/NN-slug.md` gives status only "R (state + names next unexecuted)".
findings.why_it_matters: Status now grades a plan against a contract rule the spec never assigns it and emits a state the spec's own state table does not contain, so the single coherent view of the machine is wrong about how many plan states exist and about who reads `## Governed by`. Anyone rederiving status from the spec drops the check and restores the defect it was added to fix — status routing a user to `/scaffold-go` on a plan `go` refuses at load.
findings.fix: Add the read-set check to ARCHITECTURE's `/scaffold-status` section (one sentence: status greps the finalized plan for a non-empty `## Governed by` or the verbatim `Governed by: none` line plus a per-path existence check, reports *read-set malformed* ahead of *final & fresh*, and routes to `/scaffold-plan --final`, leaving whether the entries are the *right* ones to audit); extend the `Plan state` row with the malformed/read-set-broken state; and update the status cell of the phase-plan table row.

findings.summary: Checkpoint's coherence item 5 (~line 346-349) says plan-set coherence "is defended at finalize by `/scaffold-plan`'s neighbour check — a second home for it here would be exactly the duplication the one-home rule forbids", naming one enforcer, while contracts/phase-plan.md (line 217) and ARCHITECTURE (line 283-289) both name two: `plan`'s neighbour check *and* `/scaffold-audit`'s reality pass, which audit implements (Step 3, "Plan-set coherence within a milestone").
findings.why_it_matters: Checkpoint is the skill that disposes of audit findings; a checkpoint agent holding an audit plan-set-overlap finding reads its own text as saying the invariant has exactly one home at finalize and that a second grader is forbidden duplication — grounds to dismiss the finding rather than route it, and grounds for a maintainer to delete audit's check as a one-home violation. Audit's is also the only enforcer that can see an overlap in a pre-written milestone where no plan is being finalized.
findings.fix: Amend checkpoint's item 5 to name both enforcers — "defended at finalize by `/scaffold-plan`'s neighbour check and graded read-only after the fact by `/scaffold-audit`'s reality pass" — and narrow the rationale to why *checkpoint* is not a third home (it neither authors plans nor spins the fresh graders), rather than asserting a single home.

findings.summary: The finalize pass never tells the agent to read the milestone folder — neither to list `phases/` nor to open `milestone.md` — yet the neighbour check's sibling set and its unticked/unlisted test are computed entirely from both.
findings.why_it_matters: Read cold, the finalize pass has exactly two read instructions: step 1 ("read the files and patterns the plan's `## Scope` implies" — code only) and step 3's candidate listing of `knowledge/` + `decisions/`. Step 3 states outright that "this pass runs *instead of* Phase 1's triage, so nothing else has put those two folders in front of you" — which is equally true of the milestone folder. Step 2 then demands "every **unexecuted** sibling plan in this milestone" where unexecuted = "its `milestone.md` `## Phases` entry is unticked, **or the plan has no entry there yet**": the first half needs `milestone.md` open, and the second half is only observable by listing `phases/` and diffing it against the checklist. An agent must invent both reads, and an agent that instead derives the sibling set from the checklist alone (the only file the step actually names) systematically misses the just-authored, unlisted sibling the step calls "exactly the overlap risk this check exists for".
findings.fix: Open step 2 with the read it depends on, e.g.: "**First, list the milestone's plan set.** List `.scaffold/milestones/NN-slug/phases/` and read that milestone's `milestone.md` `## Phases` checklist. The sibling set is every plan file in `phases/` other than this one whose checklist entry is unticked, plus every plan file with no entry at all. (This pass replaces Phase 1's triage, so nothing else has put the folder in front of you.)"

findings.summary: Steps 3 and 4 say "Write `## Governed by`" / "Write `## Targets`" while step 8 says "On confirmation, write the plan" — the pass never states whether steps 3–5 edit the file on disk or compose a proposal, and step 2's hard-stop rule only makes sense under one of the two readings.
findings.why_it_matters: Both readings are defensible and they diverge on disk. Under "compose then write at 8", step 2's mandate — "Either stop above can fire while the file already carries `## Targets` — written by step 4 of this pass … **Delete `## Targets` before you stop**" — is incoherent for the fresh-finalize case (nothing was written, nothing to delete), and an agent will skip the deletion on a *re*-finalize too, leaving the previous finalize's stamp intact: precisely the abandoned-mid-finalize plan that reads *final & fresh* to `go` and executes the unresolved overlap. Under "write at 3–4", the file is stamped `## Targets` and presented to `go`/`status` as final *before* the step 7 approval seam the skill calls "the approval seam; `go` executes afterward without re-approving" — so a context loss between step 4 and step 7 leaves a finalized, never-approved plan on disk. Nothing in the skill lets a cold agent pick.
findings.fix: State the disk contract once at the top of the pass: steps 2–6 edit the plan file in place (which is why the hard stops must delete `## Targets`), and step 8's write is limited to `state.md` plus any change step 7's dialogue produced. Add the missing companion rule for the in-place reading: if the pass is abandoned before step 7's confirmation, delete `## Targets` — same treatment as a hard stop.

findings.summary: The neighbour check deliberately puts thin, just-authored drafts in reach, then gates every hit on naming "the one artifact" both items leave in the same end state — something a code-blind draft almost never names — with no instruction for what to do when the sibling is too vague to answer the subtraction test.
findings.why_it_matters: Step 2 reaches siblings with no `## Phases` entry because "a just-authored sibling is exactly the overlap risk this check exists for", and those siblings are drafts by definition — the skill's own draft definition is "high-level, code-blind". The subtraction test is then run "if that sibling executed first, **exactly as written**", and admission requires naming a file/table/column/test/document/procedure/dataset. A draft that says "stand up the export pipeline" names no artifact, so a cold agent applying the bar literally records "can't name it → there is no finding" for every draft sibling and the check reports zero hits on exactly the population it was built for. The alternative reading — resolve the vagueness by asking the user or by reading code — is forbidden by the same step ("no code is read for this step"). Nothing in the skill says which.
findings.fix: Add the missing branch after the admission bar, e.g.: "**A sibling too thin to answer the test is not a pass.** If a draft sibling's `## Objective`/`## Scope` cannot be reduced to named artifacts, you cannot clear or admit the item on the text — say so, name the sibling and the item, and ask the user whether the sibling covers it. An unanswerable comparison is surfaced at step 7 like a hit, never silently dropped."

findings.summary: Step 3 has `go` present scope and say "Starting now." and only *then* read `## Governed by` — whose three stop conditions (dangling path, empty section, neither form) are load-time refusals `status` advertises as "`go` refuses it at load".
findings.why_it_matters: Following the step in written order, a user with a malformed read-set gets "Phase: 07-splits, final & fresh. … 4 scope items to execute. Starting now." immediately followed by "This plan carries no `## Governed by` … Re-finalize" — a refusal issued after a commitment, which is the exact pattern this skill elsewhere calls out as training users to dismiss its gates. Worse for a cold reader: the read-set paragraph sits *after* the start announcement and is qualified only by "before the first deliverable", which reads as license to defer it into Step 4 and interleave reading with building, so the contradiction stop can fire with code already written — contradicting its own "build nothing further" / "Nothing built" wording.
findings.fix: Move the read-set paragraph (and its four bullets) ahead of the "Present scope and confirm the start" paragraph in Step 3, so all three refusals fire before anything is announced, and change "before the first deliverable" to "before you present the scope".

findings.summary: For a whole hit against a *draft* sibling the step offers two opposite moves — "keep it here and drop it from the sibling, or drop it here" — with no rule for choosing, and no check that the losing phase can still be built in execution order.
findings.why_it_matters: The finalized-sibling paragraph supplies a preference ("Prefer a this-plan-only move where one is legal"), but the draft case — the common one, since siblings are meant to stay drafts — supplies none, so two agents finalizing the same pair route ownership opposite ways. The concrete failure is ordering: finalizing phase 09 against draft phase 07, an agent that "keeps it here and drops it from the sibling" hands ownership of a deliverable to the phase that runs *second*, and 07 then executes first against a scope from which the item was deleted. Nothing in the step mentions phase order at all, and the subtraction test's counterfactual ("if that sibling executed first") is explicitly order-blind, so the agent has no cue that order matters.
findings.fix: Add an ownership rule to the "No, not at all" resolution: the item goes to whichever phase must have it first — by default the lower-numbered plan — and after any drop, state that the losing plan's remaining scope still stands on its own at the point it executes; if it does not, the resolution is wrong and the seam (or a re-cut) is the answer.

findings.summary: `plan` rules the section and the `Governed by: none` sentence mutually exclusive, but every reader tests them as an inclusive or, so a plan carrying a populated `## Governed by` *and* a leftover `Governed by: none` line in `## Approach` passes audit, `go` and `status`.
findings.why_it_matters: Audit grades "either the `## Governed by` section is present **with at least one entry** or `## Approach` carries the contract's fixed line **verbatim**" — satisfied by both; `go` branches on the section first and never looks at `## Approach`; `status` checks "non-empty `## Governed by` **or** … this line verbatim". Only `plan` is told to delete the stale form, and only on a re-finalize it happens to run. So a plan that once bound nothing and now binds `tenancy.md` keeps a sentence asserting "no `knowledge/` or `decisions/` document constrains this phase" sitting in the section `go` is instructed to execute from, indefinitely and with a clean audit grade — a false rule in the one place `go` is told the rules live.
findings.fix: In audit's `## Governed by` bullet make the test exclusive: "exactly one of the two forms is present — a populated section **or** the verbatim line, never both; both present is malformed (the sentence contradicts the section `go` reads). Route to `plan` to re-finalize." Mirror the same wording in `status`'s **Read-set intact?** bullet and its read-set-broken routing line.
